page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn9ge.64xlarge is an accelerator-oriented bare-metal server in the Compute Optimized with GPU family, built to handle massive parallel processing tasks. Driven by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9A75 processors operating at 3.3 GHz, the system provides 256 dedicated vCPUs alongside 2304.0 GB of system RAM, which yields 9.0 GB of memory per core. Operating on a KVM hypervisor architecture, the instance delivers high compute density at the host processor level.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by 8 NVIDIA Blackwell architecture GPUs featuring a combined 576 GB of GPU VRAM. Inter-node communication and data ingestion are supported by a high-throughput baseline network bandwidth of 380 Gbps. The server does not bundle any local storage, meaning all data persistence and operating system disks must be provisioned via external network-attached storage services.

In terms of resource architecture and cost efficiency, aggregating eight enterprise Blackwell accelerators and 2.3 TB of host system memory within a single node minimizes inter-host communication bottlenecks during complex distributed processing. However, the reliance on external network storage requires adequate network-attached volumes to match the rapid I/O throughput required by the accelerators and high-speed network interfaces.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn9ge.64xlarge is designed for distributed deep learning model pre-training, large language model inference clusters, massive high-performance computing simulations, and GPU-accelerated scientific research pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn9ge.64xlarge is a high-density, GPU-accelerated bare-metal instance designed for demanding artificial intelligence and parallel computing workloads. It is equipped with 256 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9A75 processors clocked at 3.3 GHz, combined with 2304.0 GB of system memory at 9.0 GB per core. The server integrates 8 NVIDIA Blackwell generation GPUs offering a total of 576 GB of VRAM, supported by a 380 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. It includes no local storage, relying on external network-attached storage for disk operations. With massive GPU density and extensive memory capacity, this instance is configured for large language model training, high-throughput distributed inference, and high-performance computing pipelines.
